title: Can You...?
description: Ask about and state basic abilities with can.
objectives: Ask about and state basic abilities with can.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to ask about and state basic abilities with can. The central language is can/can't and ability questions. It belongs to the practical context of free time & abilities. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the can you...? exchange.

blocks.english: Yes, I can, but I can't dive.
blocks.explanation: This can you...? model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you like to do?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the can you...? exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Can you swim?” and “Yes, I can, but I can't dive.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: can/can't and ability questions.
